title: Vertical vs horizontal scaling

kcs.statement: Vertical scaling adds CPU, memory or disk to one machine; it needs no code changes but hits a hardware ceiling and leaves that one machine as a point of failure.
Horizontal scaling adds more machines that share the load; capacity grows by adding nodes, but the application must tolerate any request landing on any node.
Scaling up is often the sensible first step because state stays on one machine; scaling out becomes necessary when one machine's capacity at peak QPS, or its availability, is no longer enough.

problem_ideas: A database server is at 85% CPU on 16 cores and the largest instance has 128 cores: how much headroom does scaling up buy, and what does it not fix?
